steps.b:
p% means p hundredths. p% of x = (p/100) · x.

  • Increase by p%: multiply by (1 + p/100). +20% → ×1.2
  • Decrease by p%: multiply by (1 − p/100). −20% → ×0.8
  • What percent is a of b: (a/b) · 100%.
  • The whole, if p% of it is a: a : (p/100).
+20% then −20% isn’t back to the start: 1.2 · 0.8 = 0.96, so you’re 4% lower.

A ratio (razmera) a : b compares two quantities. A proportion (proporcija) says two ratios are equal:

a : b = c : d ⇒ a·d = b·c
  • Direct proportion: more of one → more of the other (more kg → higher price).
  • Inverse proportion: more of one → less of the other (more workers → fewer days). The product stays constant.
Mass percent, concentrations and stoichiometry are all percentages and proportions. If you can do “15% of 80” and “3 : x = 12 : 20” without thinking, chemistry calculations become easy.

steps.q: A 250 g rock sample contains 40 g of quartz. What percent is quartz?
A price of 500 din rises by 20%. New price?
